newsitem.title: COMOROS: OAU team meets secessionists in Comoros.
newsitem.headline: OAU team meets secessionists in Comoros.

text.p: An Organisation of African Unity (OAU) delegation met secessionist leaders on the smallest island in the Comoros Indian Ocean archipelago on Wednesday and later returned to the capital of Moroni.

Government soldiers intercepted the OAU team on arrival on Moheli and drove them to a meeting with Comoran Justice Minister Ali Hassanaly, who lives on the island, angering secessionist supporters who had turned out to welcome them, witnesses said.

They said the OAU team led by Pierre Yere of Ivory Coast saw Hassanaly shortly after being welcomed at Moheli's airport by secessionist leader Said Mohamed Souef, elected "president" on Monday by supporters.
But after their meeting with Hassanaly the OAU delegation held talks on the Comoran crisis with Souef and other secessionist leaders before returning to the Comoran capital.

"The OAU team agreed to organise a conference to bring together the government and the secessionists from Moheli and Anjouan in a neutral place," a secessionist leader, who declined to be identified, later told Reuters by telephone.
Anjouan, the second largest island in the Federal Islamic Republic of Comoros, broke away in early August after weeks of unrest. The Comoro Islands have a population of some 670,000 people.
The delegation had arrived on Moheli on Wednesday from Anjouan, where secessionist leaders on Tuesday told the OAU mediators their decision to leave Comoros was irreversible.

Islanders on Anjouan, and Moheli, say they want to return to French rule or become independent because they have received little from the government but poverty and numerous coups since Comoran independence from France in 1975.
The poverty in the three islands of Comoros contrasts with comparative prosperity on the island of Mayotte, which voted against independence in 1975 and remains under French rule.
The secessionists said they rejected the OAU delegation's insistence that they respect the integrity of the republic.
The Anjouan separatists demanded the withdrawal of troops and proposed talks in Mauritius with the Comoran government.
On Tuesday, the Chinese-built former presidential palace on the main island of Grand Comoro was burned down and one suspect was arrested. The former palace was used for government offices.

The Comoros embassy in Paris denied on Tuesday government troops would intervene on Anjouan and Moheli and said authorities in Moroni wanted to negotiate peacefully with the separatists to create a more decentralised administration.

Embassy spokesman Mohamed Wadaane admitted the federal system set up at independence had failed and the economy was in crisis. He said the Comoros must decentralise and allow other islands to elect governors and have more control over finances.
President Mohamed Taki announced a plan for more autonomy this month but separatist leaders said it did not go far enough.
